note: Continuous and discrete facts per NVIDIA board, keyed by PCI product id: what a chip is, never what it should run (docs/maintainer/gpu-facts.md). boost_mhz is the reference clock: the published boost clock of NVIDIA's reference board (laptops: the top of the published range; boost_min_mhz: its bottom, the clock a laptop is priced at), the value the CUDA driver reports as the peak SM clock of a stock board. gbps is the memory data rate per pin; bandwidth = gbps x bus_bits / 8. tdp_w: total board power (laptops: the top TGP without Dynamic Boost). vram_gib: the marketed capacity. pcie: the highest generation the board's link supports. IDs: pci-ids.ucw.cz.
archs_note: Per compute capability, the SM limits the engine uses today. smem_per_block_optin_kib, smem_per_sm_kib, max_threads_per_sm, max_blocks_per_sm and registers_per_sm are what the engine decides with (core/device_class.cpp, core/mmq_columns.h); they were written down once in those places and moved here unchanged, and they are NOT all checked: a row's checked field names the cards whose driver (cudaDeviceGetAttribute) reported all four of its limits, and the rest wait for a card; a row's source field names the published figures its limits follow where no card was read (cc 87, 107, 110 and 121: the CUDA programming guide's table and the toolkit's own architecture traits; the guide's merged cells put 1024 threads and 16 blocks on 10.7, 1536 and 24 on 11.0; the Volta row's figures, which the guide's 13.x edition no longer lists, are also those of cuda::arch_traits sm_70 and the 12.x guide). build_smem_per_block_optin_kib and build_smem_per_sm_kib are the limits kernels are compiled against (ops/common/arch_limits.h), the device figures (for sm_90..sm_119 since #648, from the guide: the tiles above 99 KiB this admits have run on GA100, not on these chips), except the rows of no chip at 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4, which compile as Volta. smem_reserved_per_block is the bytes of an SM the driver keeps per resident block (from sm_80). A row covers cc to cc_to (default: cc alone). The row with cc 0 is what a capability this table lacks gets. The consumers (core/arch_registry.h) read these rows and hold no copy.
